analysis_md:
# PSO — Pearson plc
Engine 5.5 run, 2026-10-19. In scope (market cap $12.011B at $18.19, nasdaq_quote_api). All figures below are copied from key_numbers.md, dcf_numbers.json or financials_history.csv — none are recomputed.

## What it is
The world's largest education company (London-listed, NYSE ADSs 1:1 with ordinary shares): assessments and qualifications, virtual schools, higher-education courseware, English language learning and enterprise skills. FY2025 sales £3,577m by segment (Annual Report 2025): Assessment & Qualifications £1,604m, Higher Education £775m, Virtual Learning £511m, English Language Learning £405m, Enterprise Learning & Skills £282m; ~67% of sales in the US. Underlying sales growth +4% in FY2025 and +4% in H1 2026, adjusted operating margin 17.2% in FY2025.

## Owner's earnings
Reporting currency GBP, converted to USD at period-end ECB rates (FX_CONVERTED, below). Conservative OE = OCF − total capex − SBC, with capex from the filing override (see OVERRIDE):
- FY2023: OCF $667,537,500 − capex $170,381,000 − SBC $50,860,000 = **OE $446,296,500 = $0.62/share**
- FY2024: OCF $785,568,300 − capex $167,888,600 − SBC $55,127,600 = **OE $562,552,100 = $0.82/share**
- FY2025: OCF $883,369,600 − capex $180,444,400 − SBC $52,517,400 = **OE $650,407,800 = $0.99/share**
- OE positive 5 of the last 5 fiscal years. The maintenance definition (NI + D&A − min(capex, D&A) − ΔNWC) is not in the computed outputs — the filing carries no engine-readable D&A series (used_tags.da is null) — so the conservative OCF-based definition is the base, as throughout the sweep.
- **Base used = median of the last 3 FY OE/share: $0.82/share** (base_source: median_of_last_3_fy_oe_per_share). The latest FY ($0.99/share) is NOT used as the base: FY2025 operating cash flow is flattered by the State Aid tax recovery — cash tax paid was £2m in FY2025 vs £119m in FY2024 (FY2025 20-F cash flow statement; the FY2025 results release puts the recovery at ~£0.1bn) — so the median year (FY2024) is the cleaner anchor. No TTM base: ttm.py cannot build one for this IFRS filer (it reads US-GAAP facts only and exited with no annual facts), per the worker spec the median base stands.
- Balance sheet (latest FY, CSV): cash $448,417,800, total debt $1,994,314,600, **net debt $1,545,896,800 = 2.85× normalized OE** (diagnostics), plus lease liabilities $643,674,800 not in net debt. The balance sheet also carries a £518m retirement-benefit (pension surplus) asset (Annual Report 2025) that the model does not credit.

## OVERRIDE — capex (filing, bounded authority step 8a)
- **The gap:** the preliminary run exited with `DATA_GAP:capex` — no tier. EDGAR companyfacts carries `PurchaseOfPropertyPlantAndEquipmentClassifiedAsInvestingActivities` only through FY2021; from FY2022 Pearson files PPE purchases inside the combined line "Purchase of property, plant and equipment and investment property", which no engine candidate tag reads. Intangible purchases stay tagged every year (£90m FY2022, £96m FY2023, £91m FY2024, £105m FY2025) but are not added on an assumed-zero row.
- **The decision:** judgment.json carries `capex_override = {value: 134000000, kind: "filing", currency basis: declared in GBP, engine-converted}` — the filer's TOTAL FY2025 capex from the FY2025 Form 20-F (filed 2026-03-13) consolidated cash flow statement: PP&E and investment property £29m + intangible assets £105m = £134m. Because the override is the total line, the filed intangible purchases are correctly not stacked on top (OVERRIDE_APPLIED:capex names them). Per the system's single-value convention the latest filed year fills every missing period: exact for FY2025, and it overstates FY2024 (true £124m = £33m + £91m) by ~8% and FY2023 (true £126m = £30m + £96m) by ~6% — conservative in direction. Band check (override_checks): £134m is 2.09× the last value filed under the PPE-only tag (£64m, FY2021) and 0.76× the last filed total capex (£176m, FY2021) — in band either way; the engine records out_of_band: false.
- **Measured impact (dcf_numbers.json override_impact, final scenario inputs):** zero-fill base $1.07/share → **$0.82/share** with the override; zero-fill weighted IRR 10.07% → **8.39%**. Without the override the run's OE was overstated by ~30% on a capex line that is only ~4% of sales — the override is the whole difference between the fake Tier C the zero-fill arithmetic implied and this Tier D.

## ADS ratio
20-F filer: judgment.json carries `ads_ratio = {ratio: 1}` — each ADS represents one ordinary share of 25 pence, as stated in the filer's own FY2025 Form 20-F (filed 2026-03-13), Item 12, 'Description of securities other than equity securities — American Depositary Shares': 'Each ADS represents one ordinary share.'. Per-share figures are per ordinary share and the price is per ADS; at a 1:1 ratio they are already comparable and the market cap is price × shares ($12.011B) with no scaling (ADS_RATIO_APPLIED ×1.0).

## Moat: 5/10 — moderate / narrow
Evidence first (fundamentals.json, GBP): roic_proxy FY2019–FY2025 ran 3.9% / 7.6% / 3.0% / 4.0% / 7.9% / 9.3% / 7.7% — improving, but never durably above ~10%, i.e. around the cost of capital, not well above it through a cycle. Gross margin 47–52% over the same years, 52.0% in FY2025. A moat above 6 is not supported by those returns.
- FOR: regulated assessment franchise — the Pearson VUE global test-centre network and government/professional certification contracts are hard to replicate; accredited qualifications with institutional lock-in — UK GCSE/A-levels, BTEC and the PTE English test are embedded in school, university and immigration systems; content and assessment IP plus data scale across five segments; proven pricing — underlying sales +4% in FY2025 and H1 2026 with the adjusted operating margin expanding to 17.2%.
- AGAINST: ROIC history is mediocre (above); Higher Education courseware is in structural decline — print erosion, Inclusive Access price pressure, AI tools substituting for paid courseware and study help; contract re-bid risk — US Student Assessment lost the New Jersey contract and government contracts re-tender; English Language Learning is exposed to migration policy (H1 2026 ELL guidance was cut on softer migration-driven demand) and consumer apps pressure the category.
- A 5 gives CAP = 8.5 years: growth holds 2 years, then converges linearly to the 2.5% terminal rate over 8.5 years, 15-year projection.

## Flags — every fragility flag resolved
- **DATA_GAP:capex** (preliminary run): resolved by the filing override — see OVERRIDE. data_gap_uncovered is empty in the final run.
- **ADS_RATIO_MISSING** (preliminary run): resolved — ads_ratio 1 declared from the filer's own 20-F (see ADS ratio); the final run carries ADS_RATIO_APPLIED ×1.0.
- **STALE_FY** (latest FY ended 2025-12-31, 9.6 months ago): no TTM is buildable for an IFRS filer (ttm.py reads US-GAAP facts only and exited with none) — the median base stands, per spec. Cross-check since FY end: H1 2026 interims (six months to 2026-06-30) printed underlying sales +4%, adjusted operating profit +14% underlying to £276m and reiterated FY2026 guidance — performance since the FY end supports, and does not undermine, the median base.
- **BUYBACK_TAILWIND** (share count −3.81%/yr, 742.0M → 660.3M over FY2022–FY2025): already credited via the +3.81pp growth adjustment in the blend; not double-counted in the verdict. The £350m buyback was completed in H1 2026 and a further £350m programme launched — the tailwind is real but it is in the model once.
- **OE_VOLATILE** (OE/share range over the last 5 years spans >3×: $0.22 in FY2021 to $0.99 in FY2025): the span is a COVID-trough FY2021, a genuine OCF recovery, a shrinking share count and the FY2025 tax recovery — handled by the median base (not the latest year) and by widening bear-or-worse probability to 40%.
- **NI_OCF_DIVERGENCE** (2025): net income $452,457,600 vs OCF $883,369,600. In the filing's GBP terms (profit for the year £336m vs net cash generated from operating activities £656m): the gap is non-cash charges — depreciation and impairment on PPE £54m, software amortisation and impairment £112m, acquired-intangible amortisation £41m, and product-development amortisation and impairment £364m (including the £87m one-off impairment of legacy product-development assets on platform convergence) against £285m of capitalised product-development spend — plus cash tax paid of only £2m (vs £119m in FY2024) on the State Aid recovery, while the tax charge runs through the income statement. The OCF-based conservative OE used throughout already sits downstream of all of this; the one live consequence is that FY2025 OE is flattered, which is why the base is the median year, not FY2025.
- **FX_CONVERTED**: GBP reporting converted at period-end ECB rates (1.2715 / 1.2529 / 1.3466 for FY2023/24/25, recorded in dcf_numbers.json) — flow facts use period-end, not average, rates. The visible distortion (USD revenue +8.2% YoY vs +1% in GBP) is handled in the growth recalibration above.
- **ADS_RATIO_APPLIED**: ratio 1.0 — no scaling; see ADS ratio.
- **OVERRIDE_APPLIED:capex**: see OVERRIDE — the override is the filer's total capex line, so the filed intangible purchases (£90m/£96m/£91m/£105m, FY2022–FY2025) were correctly not added on top; impact measured in dcf_numbers.json and the registry.
- **WIDE_SCENARIO_SPREAD** (super-bull IV 4.49× super-bear IV): real — the range runs from contract-loss decline to an AI-verification re-rating. Confidence is capped at medium and the verdict is sized to the bear end.
- **TIER_BAND** (bear tier D at 6.49% vs bull tier C at 10.23%): sized to the bear end — the weighted result (8.39%) is itself Tier D, and even the bull case does not reach the 15% hurdle, so the band does not change the verdict.

## My thoughts / overlay
- The honest headline is the price, not the business. Pearson is a decent, improving franchise — sales growing mid-single digits underlying, margins expanding, £527m of FY2025 free cash flow, disciplined buybacks — priced at $18.19 for an owner's-earnings stream whose normalized base is $0.82/share, a 4.5% OE yield with 2.85× net debt on top. At that yield the market is already paying for the bull case.
- Method range: the zero-fill preliminary arithmetic (capex silently $0) implied a $1.07 base and a ~10.1% weighted IRR on these same scenario inputs (Tier C) — every step of that gap is the missing capex line, now filed, cited and measured. There is no defensible method on the current filings that gets this name to a 15% hurdle at $18.19; even the super-bull scenario tops out at a 13.89% IRR.
- What would change the answer: a price near the weighted IV@15% ($8.27), or evidence that the enterprise/AI assessment opportunity lifts underlying growth durably above the mid-single-digit guide. The H1 2026 print (+4% sales, +14% adjusted operating profit) is progress, not that evidence yet.
- Watch items: FY2026 tax normalization (FY2025's £2m cash tax will not repeat — the base already uses the pre-recovery median year), US Student Assessment contract renewals after the New Jersey loss, ELL demand under tighter migration policy, and whether Higher Education stabilizes at its FY2025 +2% underlying growth.

## Final verdict
- **Final tier: D** (weighted IRR 8.39%; sized to the bear end per TIER_BAND — bear 6.49%, bull 10.23%)
- Confidence: **Medium** (filing-sourced override and resolved flags; capped by WIDE_SCENARIO_SPREAD and the unavailability of a TTM base for an IFRS filer)
- One-liner: Improving global education franchise with a regulated assessment moat, moat 5/10 — but at $18.19 it does not clear 15%: Tier D, weighted IRR 8.39%, weighted IV@15% $8.27; it clears the hurdle only below ~$8.27, less than half the current price.
